title: Every refinement whose verify passes crashes in judgeStep: refine builds have no brief
failureScenario: The owner sends a refinement such as "add a dark mode". insertRefineBuild (lib/pipeline/records.ts:71) inserts the build row without a brief, and the comment at build-steps.ts:673 confirms that refine rows have none. refineProduct -> checkAndFix -> verify passes -> judgeStep -> loadBuild(refine build) -> requireBrief(build) throws FatalError("This build has no brief yet."). The error is not retried, refineProduct's catch calls failStep, and the refinement ends as failed even though the change was good. The scenario tests mock judgeStep, so they never hit this. Second problem: judgeStep passes the refinement inspiration's references, which are only the new prefixed files. judgeBuild then pairs them with the original brief's reference indexes and gives the judge the wrong descriptions.
suggestedFix: In judgeStep, use `build.brief ?? await latestBrief(build.productId)`, as startDeployStep does. Pass the references of the product's original build inspiration (or none) instead of the refinement's new-only list. Add a scenario test for kind "refine" that runs the real judgeStep.
fixNotes: In judgeStep: `const brief = build.brief ?? (await latestBrief(input.productId)); if (!brief) throw new FatalError(...)`. For kind "refine", pass the references of the product's original inspiration (`(await loadInspiration((await loadProduct(build.productId!)).inspirationId)).references`), so they line up with the original brief's indexes. Add a refine scenario that runs the real judgeStep against a stubbed judgeBuild.

title: Refinements skip the policy gate, and the refine prompt tells Muse Code to build the closest version of disallowed requests
failureScenario: A user ships a harmless product, then sends a refinement: "make it look exactly like Chase's sign-in page and add username and password fields". Refinements never pass through the brief writer's refusal check, which only runs in briefStep. The message goes verbatim into refine-N.md. renderRefinePrompt line 322 says: "If the request is something AGENTS.md says not to build ... build the closest useful version". That directly contradicts AGENTS.md:69 ("don't build it... stop"). AGENTS.md:69 also leaves out brand cloning, collecting credentials or payment details, and targeting a private person, which the brief writer does refuse. Muse Code builds it. The judge may fail it for copying a real product's look, but brief-template-2 ships it as partial anyway, and the brief-template-1 crash means a refinement whose verify fails but builds also ships as partial.
suggestedFix: Run refinement messages (and their new references) through a Spark policy check that uses the briefInstructions refusal list before writing refine.md. If it refuses, end the build as refused. Change line 322 to say that if the request is something AGENTS.md forbids, Muse Code changes nothing, writes the reason in BUILD_NOTES.md and stops. Add brand or product cloning, credential or payment collection under false pretenses, and anything aimed at a private person to AGENTS.md:69.
fixNotes: Split render.ts:322 in two. If the request is something AGENTS.md says not to build, change nothing, write the reason in BUILD_NOTES.md and stop. If no listed model can do it, build the closest useful version. Run the refinement message (and the new references' kinds) through a Spark structured check that uses the same refusal list before reopenStep, and end the build as refused while keeping the live version. Add cloning a real brand or product, collecting passwords or payment details under false pretenses, and targeting a private person to AGENTS.md:69.

title: Daily budget and platform cap are checked before each call and never reserved, so parallel requests overshoot them many times over
failureScenario: tokenSpendToday and platformSpendToday add up rows that recordUsage writes only inside deps.defer, after the upstream body has fully drained (handler.ts:232-237). Until a request finishes, the budget check cannot see its cost, and nothing limits the cost of one request: max_output_tokens is not clamped, and input can be about 1M tokens (a 4.5 MB body, or a public Blob video URL that Meta fetches). Example: someone sends 120 parallel requests in one second to a product's public action route, each carrying about 4 MB of text for muse-spark-1.3 (about $1.25 each). The per-token limit allows 120 per minute, and the per-IP limit never applies (gateway-2). All 120 pass `spent >= 3` and `platformSpent >= 40` while spent is still $0. The result is about $150 in one burst against a $3 product budget and a $40 platform cap, which is the whole hackathon credit. With Wonder ($4/M input) the cost is about 3x higher. A build token ($1) in the sandbox, where untrusted generated code runs, overshoots the same way.
suggestedFix: Reserve spend before forwarding. Insert a pending usage row, or increment a per-token and per-platform in-flight counter, with a pessimistic estimate (body bytes / 4 x input price + clamped max_output_tokens x output price), reject when spent + reserved + estimate exceeds the budget, and replace the reservation with the metered cost afterwards. Also clamp or inject max_output_tokens on responses, and cap concurrent in-flight requests per token (for example 10).
fixNotes: Smallest fix: before forwarding, insert a usage row with a pessimistic estimate in the same SQL statement that checks the totals. For example, INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (token sum + estimate) <= dailyBudget AND (platform sum + estimate) <= cap, or do it under pg_advisory_xact_lock so two requests can't both pass on the same totals. Estimate as body bytes / 4 x input price plus the clamped max_output_tokens x output price. After metering, update that row to the real cost; if upstream fails, delete it. Also inject or clamp `max_output_tokens` on responses bodies, and cap in-flight requests per token (for example 10) so slow video calls can't pile up across rate windows.

title: judgeStep requires a brief on the refine build row, so every refinement that passes verify fails
failureScenario: A user refines a live product ("add a dark mode"). insertRefineBuild creates the refine build row with brief NULL, and loadRefineStep (build-steps.ts:805-808) copies only sandboxName, museSessionId and buildModel onto it. The comment on latestBrief (line 673) already says refine rows have no brief. Muse Code makes the change and npm run verify passes, so checkAndFix calls judgeStep. judgeStep runs requireBrief(build) on the refine row, which throws FatalError("This build has no brief yet."). FatalError is not retried, so refineProduct's catch calls failStep and the refine ends failed with that message. The passing change is never deployed. The only way a refinement can ship today is if verify fails every round and the run falls through to partial. The scenario tests fake judgeStep, and production has only run a new build, so nothing caught this.
suggestedFix: In judgeStep, use `build.brief ?? await latestBrief(build.productId)` (the same fallback startDeployStep uses), or have loadRefineStep copy the product's first-build brief onto the refine row. Also give the judge the original inspiration's image references plus the refine's new ones, not just the refine attachments.
fixNotes: In judgeStep: `const brief = build.brief ?? (await latestBrief(input.productId)); if (!brief) throw new FatalError(...)` and pass that brief, the same fallback startDeployStep uses. judgeBuild matches brief.inspiration.references to input.references by index, so for a refine also pass the first build's inspiration references (load them through that build's inspirationId), not the refine's own attachments. You can append the refine's new images after them.

title: Admin is granted from the typed email alone, so anyone with the shared access code can sign in as admin
failureScenario: PLATFORM_ACCESS_CODE is handed to every judge and tester. One of them POSTs /api/auth/sign-in with {email: "<the owner's address in ADMIN_EMAILS>", code}. signIn sets isAdmin = env.adminEmails.includes(email) without verifying the email and issues a 14-day cookie with adm:true. That person can now hit the kill switch on any product (POST /api/products/<slug>/status {"status":"disabled"}), start /api/rebuilds batches, refine any user's product (the isAdmin bypass in app/api/builds/[buildId]/messages/route.ts:39), and skip the daily quota. The same unverified identity lets anyone sign in as any user whose email they know and refine that user's products. It also lets anyone reset their per-user quota with a fresh email, or by firing parallel POSTs before the count (checkBuildAllowed then insertBuild is not atomic).
suggestedFix: Gate admin on a separate secret (for example ADMIN_ACCESS_CODE) or a signed magic link, never on the email claim. In requireAdmin, re-derive isAdmin from env or the DB instead of trusting the cookie's adm flag.
fixNotes: Require a separate secret for admin, for example ADMIN_ACCESS_CODE: isAdmin = adminEmails.includes(email) && safeEqual(code, env.adminAccessCode). Have rebuild-all.ts send that code. In requireAdmin, also re-check env.adminEmails.includes(user.email), so removing an email takes effect without waiting 14 days.

title: Firewall signs every api.meta.ai request in the VM with the master key, on any path and method
failureScenario: The rule `"api.meta.ai": [{ transform: [{ headers: { Authorization: Bearer <MODEL_API_KEY> } }] }]` has no `match`, so the firewall rewrites the Authorization header on every request to api.meta.ai from any process in the VM. That includes Muse Code's --yolo shell, the Playwright tests and the product's own server, which `next dev` exposes on the public sb-*.vercel.run preview URL. None of these calls go through the gateway, so they skip its endpoint and model allowlist, the budgets, the kill switch and usage metering, and DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD never counts them. Example: a muse note such as "an explorer that lists my uploaded files from https://api.meta.ai/v1/files" becomes a brief, and Muse Code writes code that calls Meta directly. Inside the sandbox that code works with the master key. If Meta mirrors OpenAI's GET /v1/files and /v1/files/{id}/content, it lists and downloads every file the platform's brief step (lib/brief/media.ts files.create) and every product gateway upload stored under that key, which includes other users' PDF and video inspo. The data can then go out through the allowed hosts: it can be baked into the product source or preview page, or PUT to an attacker's own Blob store through vercel.com/api/blob. The same hole also allows unmetered spend on the platform key, for example a curl loop to /v1/images/generations.
suggestedFix: @vercel/sandbox 3.9 supports `match` and `response` rules. Scope the injection to what Muse Code needs: method POST, path startsWith "/v1/responses" (plus GET /v1/models if the launcher needs it), and a header matcher on authorization exact "Bearer brokered". End the rule list with a catch-all `{ response: { statusCode: 403, body: "blocked", contentType: "text/plain" } }` so every other api.meta.ai request is refused instead of signed. Consider allowing vercel.com only on path /api/blob.
fixNotes: In builderNetworkPolicy, scope the brokering rule and end the list with a deny rule. The library supports this: `match` takes path, method and headers, and a trailing `response` rule with no `match` answers anything earlier rules did not claim. Example: `"api.meta.ai": [{ match: { method: ["POST"], path: { startsWith: "/v1/responses" }, headers: [{ key: { exact: "authorization" }, value: { exact: `Bearer ${placeholder}` } }] }, transform: [{ headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${key}` } }] }, { response: { statusCode: 403, body: "blocked", contentType: "text/plain" } }]`. Before locking this down, measure which endpoints Muse Code actually calls; it might use GET /v1/models or POST /v1/files for --image. Use a temporary catch-all 403 and watch muse-r0.err. "Bearer brokered" is public knowledge, so a per-sandbox random placeholder is safer. Put it only in the muse runner's env (SANDBOX_ENV in startMuse) and match on it. The dev and verify runners don't export it, so the product server's processes can't get the key injected unless Muse writes the placeholder into source. Both provision and reopen go through lockedPolicy(), so one change covers both.

title: Sign-in never checks that the person owns the email, so anyone with the shared code can sign in as an admin or as any other user
failureScenario: signIn() takes the email as the identity once the shared PLATFORM_ACCESS_CODE matches, and grants admin when that email is in ADMIN_EMAILS (lines 84-92). There is no email verification of any kind. Every tester and judge gets the same code. Any of them can POST /api/auth/sign-in with {email: <an admin's address, e.g. the organizer's public git email>, code} and get a signed cookie with adm:true. That cookie works for the kill switch (/api/products/<slug>/status, which can turn off every product during judging), for 'Rebuild all' (/api/rebuilds, which spends up to DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD), and for unlimited builds (checkBuildAllowed returns ok for any admin). Signing in as another tester's email returns that user's row from onConflictDoUpdate. That gives their /builds list and lets you refine and redeploy their live products (the messages route checks product.ownerId === user.id). Signing in as fresh made-up emails also skips the per-user daily quota completely. A related problem: requireAdmin and checkBuildAllowed trust the adm flag from the 14-day cookie and never re-read users.is_admin, so taking someone out of ADMIN_EMAILS does nothing until their cookie expires.
suggestedFix: Do not give admin based only on a claimed email. Use a separate admin secret, or a magic-link or OTP check on the email before the session is issued (at least for ADMIN_EMAILS). In requireAdmin and checkBuildAllowed, re-read users.is_admin, and compare it against the current env.adminEmails, rather than trusting the cookie's adm flag. Treat email identity as unverified for ownership checks, or verify it.
fixNotes: Smallest fix: grant admin only with a separate secret. Add ADMIN_ACCESS_CODE and set isAdmin = adminEmails.includes(email) && safeEqual(code, env.adminAccessCode); the shared code alone never grants admin. In requireAdmin, and in checkBuildAllowed before skipping the quota, call loadUser(user.id) and require row.isAdmin && env.adminEmails.includes(row.email), ignoring the cookie's adm flag. To stop impersonating other testers, verify the email (magic link or OTP) or bind identity to something the person holds. At minimum, do not reuse an existing user row on sign-in unless the request proves ownership, for example a per-user secret sent the first time.

title: Every product's /api/upload is an open, unlimited relay that hands out 200 MB public upload tokens for the platform's Blob store
failureScenario: Anyone can script POST https://musemuse-<slug>.vercel.app/api/upload with {"type":"blob.generate-client-token","payload":{"pathname":"uploads/a.mp4"}}. The proxy attaches the product's PRODUCT_TOKEN with no Origin check, no client IP and no limit. handleGatewayUpload (lib/gateway/uploads.ts:66-99) checks only that the token exists and the product isn't disabled: no hitRateLimits, no budget, no metering. It returns a client token valid for one hour, for up to 200 MB, for image/* (which includes SVG), mp4, mov, wav, pdf and text. In a loop this gives unbounded storage and bandwidth cost and anonymous public file hosting on the platform's *.public.blob.vercel-storage.com for 24 hours. The same works against any build's public sandbox preview with the build token.
suggestedFix: Rate-limit token issuance in handleGatewayUpload per token and per forwarded client IP, reusing deps.hitRateLimits. Cap the daily bytes per product. Forward x-musemuse-client-ip from the proxy and reject cross-site requests there (Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site). Lower maximumSizeInBytes to what products need, and restrict image/* to raster types.
fixNotes: In handleGatewayUpload, call deps.hitRateLimits (add it to UploadDeps) on `upload:token:<id>` and `upload:ip:<productId>:<ip>` with a small per-minute limit, plus a daily count per product. Have the template proxy forward x-musemuse-client-ip and reject cross-site requests (Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site, or an Origin that doesn't match). Replace image/* with an explicit raster list (no SVG) and lower maximumSizeInBytes.

title: Products the judge rejects for copying a brand, logo or character, or for implying Meta made them, still ship publicly as "partial"
failureScenario: The inspo is a screenshot of a real app. Muse Code keeps that app's name and logo. verify passes (all 6 steps ok). The judge fails the build under rule 3 ("shows a name, logo, character... or copies a real product's look") on the first round and on all 3 fix rounds. checkAndFix returns passed=false with steps that are all ok. finish() reads BUILD_NOTES.md, which Muse Code always writes because brief.md's 'Done means' requires it. decideOutcome sees typecheck, build and start ok and returns "partial", so ship() deploys it to musemuse-<slug>.vercel.app and registers the MCP connector. The scenario test b4 confirms this: it only fails because buildNotes:false. JudgeVerdict has no field that separates policy failures from quality failures, so the 'inspired by, never a copy' rule (DESIGN: ship partial only when 'the failure is a documented limit') is bypassed.
suggestedFix: Add a policy flag to VerdictSchema in lib/judge.ts (for example `copiesInspoOrBrand: boolean` and `impliesMeta: boolean`) and to JUDGE_INSTRUCTIONS. Carry it through judgeStep and checkAndFix, and make decideOutcome return "failed" when the last judge run set it. Better still, allow "partial" only when the judge never ran or failed only for missing features.
fixNotes: Add a `breaksRules: boolean` field (rules 3 and 4) to VerdictSchema, JudgeVerdict and JUDGE_INSTRUCTIONS. Return it from judgeStep, have checkAndFix carry the last judged round's value, and make decideOutcome return "failed" when it is true. Also cover the never-judged path: before allowing partial, run the judge on whatever screenshots the last verify saved, or fail when no judge run has cleared policy.

title: The demo recording reuses whatever server is on port 3100, which can be a stale build, and the video is published even when the run failed
failureScenario: `npm run demo` doesn't set MUSEMUSE_PORT, so the demo runs against port 3100 with reuseExistingServer: true. The template's own `npm start` binds 3100. verify.mjs spawns its server with detached:true (line 209), so when Muse Code's shell tool times out and kills a long `npm run verify` it started during a fix round, the `next start -p 3100` child survives as an orphan in its own process group. A plain `npm start &` left by Muse Code has the same effect. The platform's verify picks 3101 and passes against the fresh build. ship() then runs demo, Playwright sees 3100 answering and reuses the stale server. That server serves the pre-fix UI, or 500s because verify's `next build` replaced the .next it loaded. finishDemo never checks run.status, so the MP4 of the stale or failed run is published as the product's demo.
suggestedFix: Have the demo pick a free port and pass MUSEMUSE_PORT (for example a `node scripts/verify.mjs --demo` mode that starts its own server). Set reuseExistingServer only when MUSEMUSE_PORT is set, or kill any listener on 3100 before the demo. In finishDemo, skip the video when run.status isn't "passed".
fixNotes: In finishDemo, return {videoUrl:null} unless run?.status === "passed" (or check the demo exit code in ship()). For the demo task, export MUSEMUSE_PORT set to a free port, using verify's pickPort logic, in startTask's runner, or set `reuseExistingServer: Boolean(process.env.MUSEMUSE_PORT)` and give the demo its own port.

title: Template helpers never send x-musemuse-client-ip, so the gateway's per-IP rate limit never applies and one visitor can drain a product's daily budget
failureScenario: The gateway applies the 20/min per-IP limit only when the product forwards its end user's IP in x-musemuse-client-ip (handler.ts:45-60, policy.ts:34). Nothing in the template sets that header: metaClient() has no defaultHeaders, and transcribeFile and the upload proxy don't send it either. AGENTS.md doesn't mention it, so generated products never do. A single client looping POST /api/actions/<name> at the 120/min per-token cap spends the product's $3 live budget in minutes. After that, every other user (and the hackathon judges) gets 429 budget_exceeded until 00:00 UTC.
suggestedFix: Give the helpers a request-aware variant (for example `metaClient(request)`, or a helper that reads x-forwarded-for / x-real-ip from next/headers) that sets x-musemuse-client-ip as a default header. Use it in transcribeFile and in app/api/upload/route.ts, and tell Muse Code in AGENTS.md and meta-reasoning to always pass the request.
fixNotes: Give metaClient an optional client IP (for example `metaClient(ip?: string)` plus a `clientIp(request)` helper reading the first x-forwarded-for entry or x-real-ip, which Vercel sets). Set `defaultHeaders: {"x-musemuse-client-ip": ip}`, use it in transcribeFile and app/api/upload/route.ts, and document it in AGENTS.md and the meta-reasoning skill. Consider a per-IP daily cost cap too.

title: The per-IP rate limit never applies because no product sends x-musemuse-client-ip
failureScenario: checkRateLimits adds the 20/min per-IP limit only when the request has x-musemuse-client-ip. Products must call Meta only through template/lib/meta (AGENTS.md). metaClient() (template/lib/meta/client.ts:15) builds the OpenAI client with only baseURL and apiKey, and transcribeFile sends only auth headers. AGENTS.md and the skills never mention the header. So every gateway request arrives without it, and the only limit is 120/min per token, which all visitors share. One person running a script against a product's /api/actions/<name>, or a judge's UI stuck in a retry loop, can use the full 120/min and the product's $3 daily budget. Everyone else then gets 429 budget_exceeded until 00:00 UTC, which can happen mid-demo. The test at handler.test.ts:92 sets the header by hand, so it passes while production never sends it.
suggestedFix: Make the contract real: have metaClient() and transcribeFile accept the end user's IP (from x-forwarded-for on the product's incoming request) and send it as x-musemuse-client-ip, and tell AGENTS.md to pass it. Alternatively, apply a fallback per-token concurrency or burst limit when the header is missing, so one client cannot use the whole token's capacity.
fixNotes: Have metaClient() and transcribeFile take an optional end-user IP. metaClient can pass `defaultHeaders: { 'x-musemuse-client-ip': ip }` to new OpenAI. The IP comes from the first entry of x-forwarded-for on the product's incoming request. Add one line to AGENTS.md telling action routes to pass it. As a backstop, when the header is missing, the gateway could add a small per-token concurrency or burst limit.

title: Upload tickets have no rate limit or quota, and every product's /api/upload hands them to anonymous callers
failureScenario: template/app/api/upload/route.ts forwards any POST body to {GATEWAY_URL}/uploads with the product's own token. The gateway checks only that the token is valid and the product is not disabled or failed, then signs a client token for the platform's Blob store: 200 MB maximum, valid for one hour, image/*, mp4, mov, wav, pdf or text, public access. It applies no hitRateLimits, no budget and no per-product byte quota. Anyone can loop `curl -X POST https://musemuse-<slug>.vercel.app/api/upload -d '{"type":"blob.generate-client-token","payload":{"pathname":"uploads/x.mp4","multipart":true}}'` and then upload 200 MB public files without limit, getting free file hosting on the platform's account until the hourly cron deletes them. Public sandbox previews holding a build token work the same way. Filling the Blob store or its transfer quota also breaks the platform's own inspo, screenshot and demo writes, which the build pipeline needs.
suggestedFix: In handleGatewayUpload, run the same hitRateLimits as the gateway (per token, plus per IP when forwarded) before signing, and keep a per-product daily count and byte quota for issued tickets. Lower maximumSizeInBytes by content type (for example 20 MB for images and 60 MB for WAV), shorten validUntil to a few minutes, and consider putting the productId in the pathname (uploads/<productId>/...) so abuse can be traced and purged per product.
fixNotes: In handleGatewayUpload, after the token and status check, call the same hitRateLimits with a key like `upload:<tokenId>` (for example 30/min), plus a per-IP key when one is forwarded, and return 429 when over. Shorten validUntil to about 5 minutes. Put the productId in the pathname (`uploads/<productId>/...`) so abuse can be traced and purged per product. A per-product daily ticket count can be added later.

title: Preview failure ends the build before verify and the fix rounds ever run
failureScenario: Muse Code exits (exit 1, step cap hit, or just a bad last edit) and leaves the home page with a compile or runtime error. The workflow logs "Muse Code ended with an error. Checking what it wrote." and then calls previewStep. sandbox.startPreview curls localhost:3000 for 40 s, gets 500 from next dev's error overlay, and throws (builder.ts:454). previewStep.maxRetries is 1, so after about 80 s the error reaches buildProduct's catch and the build fails with "The preview step failed: Preview did not answer 200...". checkAndFix never runs, even though verify does its own typecheck, build and start (template/scripts/verify.mjs) and a fix round is exactly the designed recovery. The same happens for refinements (line 396). A product whose "/" redirects (307) can never pass preview either. A judgeStep throw (maxRetries 1, line 177) likewise fails the build instead of counting as not passed.
suggestedFix: Wrap previewStep in try/catch in both workflows: emit a log line and continue into checkAndFix, since the preview is cosmetic. Optionally retry the preview after a fix round. Treat a judgeStep error as { pass: false } with a reason so the fix loop handles it.
fixNotes: Wrap `await previewStep(...)` in try/catch in both workflows. On error, emit a log line ("The preview didn't start yet, checking anyway.") and continue into checkAndFix. Optionally call previewStep again after checkAndFix. In checkAndFix, wrap judgeStep in try/catch and treat an error as `{ pass: false }` after emitting a judge event with the reason, so writeFixPromptStep has something to show.

title: The partial gate is always open because BUILD_NOTES.md is mandatory, so failed refinements and judge-rejected builds ship
failureScenario: template/AGENTS.md ("Done means" item 3) and render.ts:88 require every run to write BUILD_NOTES.md, and the refine prompt (render.ts:323) says to add an entry. For refinements the file is already there from the first build. So buildNotesStep is effectively always true, and decideOutcome (logic.ts:57-61) returns "partial" whenever typecheck, build and start passed. (a) Refinement of a live product: the change breaks the smoke test through all 3 fix rounds, but the page still builds. The outcome is partial, so ship() deploys the broken change with target production, and registerStep sets the product to partial and revokes the old live token. The working version is replaced, although refineProduct's own failure text promises "The change did not pass its checks, so it was not deployed. The live version was kept." (b) New build: verify passes, but the judge fails every round because the product copies a real brand's logo or look. The outcome is still partial and the product is deployed publicly, so the judge never blocks anything. DESIGN says "A later layer cannot overrule an earlier failure".
suggestedFix: For refinements, ship only when checks.passed is true; otherwise keep the live version. For new builds, require that the smoke step passed and that the judge did not fail on copying. Replace the hasBuildNotes boolean with a real signal, for example a limits section written during this run (check the file's mtime against the run start or diff it), instead of the file merely existing.
fixNotes: Pass a kind or flag into finish(). For refinements, ship only when checks.passed; otherwise throw BuildStop(failedMessage) so the live version stays. For new builds, at minimum don't ship partial when the last judge verdict failed. Better, require the smoke step to have passed or the judge to have failed only on a documented limit. Replace hasBuildNotes with a signal from this run, such as BUILD_NOTES.md mtime later than the build's startedAt, read in buildNotesStep.

title: Muse Code usage is dropped when run.usage arrives on a poll that isn't final, and never recorded for runs killed at their cap
failureScenario: sandbox.pollMuse returns usage from whichever poll reads the run.usage line, and its contract says "non-empty in exactly one poll: record it when it appears" (builder.ts:348). pollMuseStep charges only when poll.done is true. Poll N: commandState's 1.2 s wait probe sees muse still exiting (flushing its session log), then readBytes reads run.usage and run.terminal.completed. Usage is non-empty but done is false, so it is discarded and the offset moves past it. Poll N+1: the command has finished, there are no new lines, usage is [], and the run's roughly $1 is never written. builds.costUsd, /usage and platformSpendToday (which drives the DAILY_SPEND_CAP kill switch) all undercount. Separately, runMuse's cap path (workflow.ts:122-128) kills the command and returns without a final poll, so a 20-minute run that hit the cap, the most expensive case, records $0.
suggestedFix: Charge whenever poll.usage is non-empty, de-duplicated per cmdId or log path, not only when done. After killStep, do one last pollMuse, or read usage from `muse export`, so killed runs are billed.
fixNotes: In pollMuseStep, charge whenever poll.usage.length is non-zero, not only when done. That is safe because the offset moves past the line once, and unrecorded() already dedupes step retries. In runMuse's cap path, run one more pollMuseStep after killStep to pick up any run.usage written on shutdown. If Muse Code writes none on SIGTERM, fall back to the session's totals from `muse export`, or record an estimate so the spend cap still sees the run.

title: startPreview throws unless GET / returns exactly 200 within 8 s, ending the build before any fix round
failureScenario: After Muse Code's first run, the workflow calls previewStep, which has 1 retry and no catch in buildProduct or refineProduct, before checkAndFix. startPreview only succeeds when curl to http://localhost:3000/ returns exactly 200. Case 1: Muse Code's code throws on first render (500), the dev server fails to start (000), or / redirects (307, since curl runs without -L). The 80-iteration loop then gives up after about 40 s, throws 'Preview did not answer 200', and the retry does the same. The build is marked failed at 'preview' and none of the three fix rounds run. This is exactly the case workflow.ts:330-331 expects ('Muse Code ended with an error. Checking what it wrote.'), and also what happens when Muse Code hits --max-model-steps mid-edit. Case 2: the home page server-renders a model call through the gateway that takes more than 8 s. Every curl hits --max-time 8 and reports 000, so the loop runs 80 x 8.5 s, about 680 s with no timeoutMs on sh(). That is past a typical function maxDuration (300 s), so the step is killed. On the retry, localStatus sees 000 again and starts a second `next dev`, which fails on the port or lock and overwrites dev.log, hiding the real error.
suggestedFix: Treat any HTTP status other than 000 as 'server is up' and return sandbox.domain(3000). Leave whether / works to verify, whose failures feed the fix loop. Use a short curl --max-time and pass a timeoutMs to the sh() call so the step stays well under the function limit. Also catch preview errors in the workflow, emit a log line and continue to checkAndFix instead of failing the build. Don't start a second dev runner when the recorded 'dev' command is still running (check runningCommand(sandbox, "dev") first).
fixNotes: In startPreview, treat any status other than "000" as "server is up" and return sandbox.domain(3000). In the wait loop, exit 0 when `$c` != 000, and leave whether / works to verify. Lower curl --max-time (for example 5) and pass timeoutMs (for example 90_000) to that sh() call so the step stays bounded. Before starting a dev runner, check `await runningCommand(sandbox, "dev")` and skip the start if one is still running. In workflow.ts, wrap both previewStep calls in try/catch: on error, emitStep a log line such as "The preview did not start; checking the build anyway." and continue to checkAndFix. A broken page then fails verify and goes into a fix round instead of failing the build.

title: Muse Code usage is dropped when run.usage is read in a poll before the process exits
failureScenario: MusePoll.usage is documented (builder.ts:346-350) as non-empty in exactly one poll, 'record it when it appears'. pollMuseStep only charges `if (poll.done && poll.usage.length)`. pollMuse checks command state first: getCommand, then a 1.2 s wait probe, which returns not finished while Muse Code is still alive. Only then does it read the log. Muse Code writes run.usage and run.terminal.completed together as its last lines (docs/spikes/muse-exec-sample.jsonl, same recorded_at) and then saves its session and exits. If those lines are flushed after the probe ends but before readBytes, while the process hasn't exited yet, the poll returns done=false with non-empty usage, which is not charged, and the offset moves past those lines. The next poll returns done=true with usage=[], so that run is never charged. The window is the readBytes round trip plus Muse's exit delay, roughly 1-2 s of each 15 s poll, so a noticeable share of runs (build plus up to 3 fix rounds) go unrecorded. Muse Code is the largest cost item (about 89k input tokens even for a two-line edit), so builds.cost and platformSpendToday() undercount, and the DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD kill switch trips late. A second path: when a run hits its cap, runMuse (workflow.ts:123) kills it and returns without a final poll, so any usage or terminal lines Muse Code writes on SIGTERM are never read.
suggestedFix: Charge whenever poll.usage is non-empty, whether or not the run is done. charge()/unrecorded() already dedupe step retries, so this is safe. After killStep in runMuse, run one last pollMuseStep from the current offset so the killed run's final lines and usage are emitted and charged.
fixNotes: In pollMuseStep, change the condition to `if (poll.usage.length)`. Double charging is not a concern: usage appears in only one poll because the offset moves past it, and a step retry re-reads from the same input offset at attempt > 1, where unrecorded() drops the already-written rows. Optional: after killStep in runMuse, call pollMuseStep once more from the current `offset` so any final lines are emitted and charged. That only recovers usage if Muse writes run.usage on SIGTERM, which nobody has verified. A killed run with no run.usage stays unmetered either way.

title: Pressing Enter twice in the muse box starts two builds
failureScenario: The textarea's onKeyDown calls submit() on every Enter. submit() (line 270) checks signedIn, hasContent, pending and failed, but never checks submitting. The textarea stays enabled while the request runs, and submitting also stays true and unchecked after success while router.push is still navigating. POST /api/inspirations is slow: checkBuildAllowed, a batch insert and the workflow start() take roughly 1-2 s, and nothing visible changes in that time except the send button's spinner. A user who presses Enter again in that window sends a second POST. There is no idempotency in insertBuild, so it creates a second inspiration and build and starts a second workflow. Each one spends about $1-3 of Meta credits and one of the user's 3 daily builds, and the user is pushed to whichever buildId came back last. The other build keeps running unseen.
suggestedFix: Return early from submit() when submitting is true, using a ref (submittingRef.current) so a second key press inside the same render is also blocked. Keep the guard set after success until navigation finishes. You could also send a client-generated idempotency key that the route dedupes.
fixNotes: Add const inFlight = useRef(false). At the top of submit(), after the signedIn check: if (inFlight.current) return; inFlight.current = true. Reset it to false only on the error paths, the ones that currently call setSubmitting(false), and leave it set after a successful router.push. Optionally also clear note on success, or disable the textarea while submitting.

title: After one failed refinement, the owner can never refine the product again from the UI
failureScenario: isLatest is props.history[0].id === build.id, where history is every build of the product ordered by startedAt (failed ones included). showRefine needs shipped && canRefine && isLatest. Example: refinement F fails its checks. The workflow says 'The live version was kept', the product stays live and latestBuildId still points at the last good build G. The product page's Refine button links to /b/G?refine=1#refine. In G's room, isLatest is false because history[0] is F, so no composer is shown, only 'A newer build of this product exists. Open it to make more changes.' That message links to F. F's status is failed, so shipped is false and F has no composer either. The owner hits a dead end, even though POST /api/builds/<G or F>/messages would accept the change (it only looks at the product's status). A refinement that runs out of fix rounds is likely during the demo.
suggestedFix: Decide refine eligibility from the product, not from the newest build. Show the composer when the product is live or partial, no build of the product is running, and this build is product.latestBuildId (or the newest shipped build). Point the 'newer build exists' link at product.latestBuildId.
fixNotes: In BuildRoom, set isLatest from the product instead of history[0]: const isLatest = product ? product.latestBuildId === build.id : (!props.history.length || props.history[0]?.id === build.id). Also require that no build in history is in a non-terminal status before showing the composer. Point the 'newer build exists' link at product.latestBuildId, not history[0].id.

title: The one-based index heuristic moves a reference's description onto the wrong file
failureScenario: With 2 references, the model describes only the second one, correctly 0-based: inspiration.references=[{index:1, describes:"second photo: a sparrow"}]. Because indexes don't include 0 and every index is between 1 and references.length, oneBased becomes true and the entry is shifted to index 0 (reproduced: output [{index:0, describes:"second photo: a sparrow"}]). briefProblems then reports index 1 as missing. If the repair reply repeats the mistake, patchBrief keeps the wrong text for reference 0 and adds a placeholder for 1, and brief.md describes inspo/<first file> as the sparrow photo. fixtures[].referenceIndex is never shifted, so the two lists also disagree.
suggestedFix: Treat indexes as 1-based only when they are exactly a permutation of 1..references.length (or include references.length). Shift fixtures[].referenceIndex the same way when the shift is applied.
fixNotes: Treat indexes as 1-based only when they include references.length, which can't be a 0-based index (or form exactly 1..N). When the shift applies, subtract 1 from each fixtures[].referenceIndex too, before the validity check at normalize.ts:101-103.

title: Photo-input products get contradictory rules: the user's photo is a required fixture but also something to leave out, and the judge isn't told it's the input
failureScenario: The canonical bird-counter muse. The real cached brief (brief-photo.json) has fixtures[0]={fromUserSample:true, referenceIndex:0} and dontCopy=["The exact pixels of the person's photo", ...]. The rendered brief.md says "Leave out: The exact pixels of the person's photo" and "Always: ... artwork and photos from the inspo". In the same file, the Sample files section says the smoke test must use fixtures/img-2041.jpg, which is that same photo. The result screen necessarily shows the photo with boxes. The judge gets briefToMarkdown (line 329), which includes 'Leaves out: The exact pixels of the person's photo' but omits fixtures and fromUserSample entirely. It also gets the inspo photo itself and a final screenshot showing that photo, and JUDGE_INSTRUCTIONS rule 3 has no exception for user-supplied inputs. So the judge can systematically fail correct photo-reading products, Muse Code can't fix that in 3 rounds without breaking the fixture rule, and the build ends as partial instead of live. scripts/dev/brief-judge.ts tested only a generated look-alike photo, never the real inspo bytes.
suggestedFix: In renderBuildPrompt, when any fixture is fromUserSample, replace the 'photos from the inspo' clause with: 'user-sample fixtures are inputs; showing them as input/result is expected; never use them as decoration'. In briefToMarkdown (or a judge-only section), list the user-sample fixtures and say they are the test input. Add an exception to lib/prompts/judge.ts rule 3 for the user's own sample shown as the product's input or result.
fixNotes: In briefToMarkdown, or a judge-only section, list the fixtures with fromUserSample and say they are the test input, expected on screen as the input or result. Add an exception to rule 3 in lib/prompts/judge.ts for the user's own sample shown as the product's input. In renderBuildPrompt, when a fromUserSample fixture exists, reword the 'Always' clause to exclude the user's samples in fixtures/ used as inputs.

title: The platform's verify gate runs scripts Muse Code can edit, with no restore or hash check
failureScenario: The platform runs `npm run verify` from PRODUCT_DIR, which means the package.json script and scripts/verify.mjs exactly as Muse Code left them. The 'Don't edit scripts/verify.mjs, playwright.config.ts or app/api/upload/route.ts' rule (AGENTS.md:28) is advisory only, and nothing in lib/sandbox or lib/pipeline rewrites or checks these files. Example: in fix round 3, renderFixPrompt tells Muse Code to 'run npm run verify again until it exits 0'. It edits playwright.config.ts (testMatch to smoke.spec only, or a longer timeout), or edits verify.mjs or the package.json verify script so it prints {"musemuse_verify":1,"passed":true,...}. parseVerifySummary accepts that line, so the mechanical and behavioral layers report pass and only the screenshot judge stands between a broken product and 'live'. A modified upload route is also deployed as is.
suggestedFix: Before every platform verify or demo run, rewrite scripts/verify.mjs, playwright.config.ts, app/api/upload/route.ts and package.json's verify, demo and start scripts from template/ (or compare hashes and fail the build). Run `node scripts/verify.mjs` directly instead of through npm.
fixNotes: In startTask, before each verify or demo run, rewrite scripts/verify.mjs, playwright.config.ts and app/api/upload/route.ts from the template (readTemplateFiles in setup.ts already reads it). Reset only the verify, demo and start entries in package.json, so dependencies Muse Code added survive, and run `node scripts/verify.mjs` directly.

title: Smoke step counts skipped or .only-filtered tests as passing, and AGENTS.md wrongly says the tests can read .env.local
failureScenario: AGENTS.md:33 says GATEWAY_URL and PRODUCT_TOKEN are in .env.local and that '`next start` and the tests read it'. Playwright does not load .env files (no dotenv in the config or the runner), and verify passes only MUSEMUSE_PORT and CI. Muse Code commonly guards real-API tests with `test.skip(!process.env.PRODUCT_TOKEN, 'needs gateway')`. Every such test is then skipped, Playwright exits 0, and verify reports smoke ok ('2 skipped'). In the same way, a `test.only` left in smoke.spec.ts silently drops tests/actions.spec.ts, because playwright.config.ts doesn't set forbidOnly (the default is false even with CI=1). Broken action routes, which the MCP connector depends on, then ship as live.
suggestedFix: Set `forbidOnly: true` in playwright.config.ts. In the smoke step, read test-results/report.json and fail when any test was skipped or fixme, or when tests/smoke.spec.ts or tests/actions.spec.ts ran zero tests. Fix AGENTS.md:33 to say only the app server reads .env.local, that tests never see PRODUCT_TOKEN, and that tests must never be guarded on it.
fixNotes: Set `forbidOnly: true` in playwright.config.ts. In the smoke step, read test-results/report.json `stats` and fail when skipped > 0 or expected === 0. Change AGENTS.md:33 to say only the app server reads .env.local and tests must never read or be guarded on PRODUCT_TOKEN.

title: An in-flight build or refine silently undoes the kill switch when it registers
failureScenario: POST /api/products/<slug>/status {"status":"disabled"} sets products.status to disabled, and the gateway, uploads and MCP then stop serving the product. Refinements check status only when they start, and the first build runs with status building. registerStep then writes `status: input.status` ('live' or 'partial') with no condition on the current status. So an admin who disables a product while a refine or its first build is running sees it come back online when that build ships. A new live token and a new deployment are also put in place, and nothing reports that the disable was undone.
suggestedFix: In registerStep, only update the status when the current status is not 'disabled' (add `ne(products.status, 'disabled')` to the update's where clause, or keep a separate killed_at or disabled flag that the gateway checks). Also make the kill switch cancel or refuse in-flight builds for that product.
fixNotes: In registerStep, add `ne(schema.products.status, 'disabled')` to the update's where clause and return early (skip the deploy bookkeeping, or revoke the new live token) when no row was updated. Optionally, check for 'disabled' in assertSpendOk or before startDeployStep so a killed product isn't deployed at all.

title: MCP tool calls follow redirects and return response bodies of any size, so the platform can be used as a proxy
failureScenario: callAction posts to {liveUrl}/api/actions/<name> using fetch's default redirect: 'follow', reads the whole body with res.text() with no size cap, and returns it to the caller. On success the full body goes into the tool result; on error, the first 2000 characters do. /api/mcp/[slug] needs no authentication, and any signed-in user can have Muse Code build a product whose action route answers 307 or 302 with a Location they choose. The platform's function then requests that URL (307 keeps the POST and the JSON body) and passes the reply back to an anonymous MCP client. A multi-GB reply can also run the platform function out of memory. The asr path guards against exactly this with redirect: 'error' (asr.ts:55), but the MCP path does not.
suggestedFix: Pass `redirect: 'manual'` (or 'error') in callAction and treat any 3xx as a tool error. Read the body with a byte cap, using a reader loop like downloadCapped (for example 1 MB), and refuse larger replies.
fixNotes: Pass `redirect: 'manual'` in callAction and return errorResult on any 3xx. Replace res.text() with a capped reader like downloadCapped (for example 1 MB), cancel the body when it goes over, and return a tool error.

title: Streams cut off by the 290 s upstream timeout, or by any error mid-stream, record no usage at all
failureScenario: The upstream fetch uses signal AbortSignal.timeout(290_000) (handler.ts:209), and that signal also aborts reading the body. A long Wonder or Spark stream (high reasoning effort over a long video) that is still running at 290 s errors on both tee branches. meterBody's catch then returns [], so no usage row is written, even though Meta billed every token generated up to that point. The same happens on any upstream reset mid-stream. That spend never counts toward the token budget, the platform cap or the /usage numbers, and the product gets a truncated stream.
suggestedFix: In the SSE path, collect partial usage as the stream goes (count output_text deltas, or record what response.created and the in-progress events show) and record an estimated row when the stream fails before a final event. Also set the upstream timeout to apply only until headers arrive, then use a separate idle timeout for the body, and keep the total under maxDuration with margin so after() can still record usage.
fixNotes: Smallest fix: in meterBody's SSE path, keep the collector outside the try. On error, record an estimate (for example from response.created plus a count of output_text.delta characters / 4 x output price, or a fixed conservative charge) rather than returning []. Separately, apply the 290 s timeout only until headers arrive (clear it after fetch resolves) and use an idle timeout for the body, so after() still has time within maxDuration 300 to record usage.

title: Cleanup runs after the build is already terminal, so it can revoke and stop a refinement that started in between
failureScenario: finish() sets the build to live (workflow.ts:282) before the finally block runs cleanupStep (workflow.ts:351). The refine route's busy check (notBusy in records.ts) only looks for builds that aren't terminal, and the Composer shows the refine box as soon as "Live" arrives, so a refinement can be inserted right away. If the refine's reopenStep mints its build token and resumes the sandbox before the old run's cleanupStep executes (workflow replay or queue delay), cleanupStep revokes every build token of the product with revokeTokens(productId, "build"), including the refine's new one, and hibernate stops the sandbox mid-refine. Muse Code dies ("exited with no exit code"), the smoke tests get 401 from the gateway, and the refine fails. The same race exists between two back-to-back refinements.
suggestedFix: Run cleanup before the terminal setStatusStep (or move the terminal status into the finally block after cleanup). Revoke only the token ids this build minted. Skip hibernate when another build of the product isn't terminal.
fixNotes: Move the terminal setStatusStep after cleanupStep: run cleanup at the end of the try path, keep the finally block for the failure path, and make cleanupStep idempotent. Or, in cleanupStep, skip revoke and hibernate when another non-terminal build of the product exists (`builds where productId = ? and id <> buildId and status not in TERMINAL`).

title: registerStep overwrites an admin's "disabled" kill switch with live or partial
failureScenario: An admin disables a product (POST /api/products/<slug>/status {"status":"disabled"}) while its refinement (or its first build) is still running. When that build ships, registerStep sets products.status = input.status unconditionally, and startDeployStep has already minted a fresh live token. The gateway serves the product again and the MCP connector comes back, so the kill switch is silently undone.
suggestedFix: In registerStep's update, keep a disabled status (`status = case when status = 'disabled' then status else <outcome> end`), or check for disabled before deploying and stop the build.
fixNotes: In registerStep's update, use `status: sql\`case when ${schema.products.status} = 'disabled' then 'disabled' else ${input.status} end\``. Better still, check for disabled in startDeployStep before minting the live token, and stop the build with a BuildStop.

title: Any signed-in user can start a showcase rebuild through rebuildOf, bypassing the admin-only /api/rebuilds
failureScenario: A tester POSTs /api/inspirations with {note: "anything", rebuildOf: "<catalog id>"}. The build and product are tagged rebuildOf, and briefStep builds the brief from rebuildRequestText plus their note. Once it is live or partial, listRebuilds picks the most recently updated shipped product, so their product becomes the /rebuilds card for Meta's demo and counts in the pitch tally. rebuildIdsTaken then makes the admin batch (npm run rebuild-all) skip that item. The UI never sends rebuildOf, so only a crafted request hits this.
suggestedFix: Accept rebuildOf only when user.isAdmin, or drop it from this route since /api/rebuilds already covers it.
fixNotes: In the inspirations route, honor rebuildOf only when user.isAdmin and return 403 otherwise, or drop the field since /api/rebuilds covers it.

title: MAX_BUILDS_PER_USER_PER_DAY only applies at a user's first sign-in
failureScenario: users.daily_build_quota is NOT NULL DEFAULT 3. signIn (auth.ts:89) writes env.maxBuildsPerUserPerDay only when it inserts the row (onConflict updates isAdmin only), and effectiveQuota always finds a number in the row, so its env fallback is dead code. If the organizer raises MAX_BUILDS_PER_USER_PER_DAY to 10 for judging day, nobody who has already signed in gets it: they still hit 429 daily_limit after 3 builds, and refinements count toward that.
suggestedFix: Make the column nullable with no default and fall back to env when it is null, or use max(row quota, env) in checkBuildAllowed, or update the column on every sign-in.
fixNotes: In checkBuildAllowed, use `Math.max(row?.quota ?? 0, env.maxBuildsPerUserPerDay)`. Or make the column nullable with no default and let effectiveQuota fall back to env when it is null. Updating the column on sign-in alone isn't enough, because sessions last 14 days.

title: safeNext can be bypassed with a tab or newline, giving an open redirect after sign-in
failureScenario: safeNext only rejects values that start with '//' or '/\'. The WHATWG URL parser removes ASCII tab, CR and LF before parsing, so the value '/\t/evil.example' passes the check. It comes from /sign-in?next=/%09/evil.example after search-param decoding. new URL('/\t/evil.example', origin) resolves to https://evil.example/ (I checked this with node). SignInForm calls router.replace(safeNext(next)) after a successful sign-in. In Next 16, sequential-router-queue.navigate builds new URL(href, location.href), isExternalURL is then true, and completeHardNavigation calls location.replace, so the victim lands on the attacker's site right after typing the shared access code. That site can then show a fake 'code expired, re-enter it' page to harvest the code. Users who are already signed in get the same redirect from the 'Continue' <Link href={next}> on app/sign-in/page.tsx:35.
suggestedFix: Parse the value and compare origins instead of checking prefixes. For example: const u = new URL(next, 'https://x.invalid'); return u.origin === 'https://x.invalid' && !u.pathname.startsWith('/sign-in') ? u.pathname + u.search + u.hash : '/'. Or reject any value that contains control characters or backslashes.
fixNotes: In safeNext, reject anything containing control characters or backslashes before the prefix checks: if (/[\u0000-\u001f\u007f\\]/.test(next)) return '/'. Or parse it: const u = new URL(next, 'https://x.invalid'); if (u.origin !== 'https://x.invalid' || u.pathname.startsWith('/sign-in')) return '/'; return u.pathname + u.search + u.hash.

title: The product iframe hands camera and microphone to every untrusted generated product, and Chrome stores the grant under Muse Muse's origin
failureScenario: Every product page embeds product.liveUrl with allow="camera; microphone; ...". These products are AI-generated from any signed-in user's muse. Under Chrome's permission delegation, a delegated iframe's prompt is shown for the top-level origin (muse-muse.vercel.app), and the grant is stored for that origin. Example: a viewer (say a judge trying the voice-memo demo) allows the microphone once inside product A's embed on /p/recipe-card. After that, any other product page they open, such as /p/<product built by another tester>, embeds a different generated app with the same delegation, and its getUserMedia succeeds with no prompt. A malicious or sloppy generated product can then record audio or video and send it off from the page. The prompt only ever named Muse Muse, never the product.
suggestedFix: Remove camera and microphone from the embed's allow list. Products that need them can be opened in their own tab with the existing Open button, where the browser prompts for the product's own origin. If an embed must keep them, enable them per product only for the owner's own view, and still remember that grants are shared across all embeds.
fixNotes: Remove camera and microphone from the iframe's allow list (keep clipboard-write and fullscreen). Products that need media can be used through the existing Open button, where the prompt names the product's own origin.

title: An unvalidated musemuse.json from a partial ship crashes the build room, product page and gallery
failureScenario: readManifest (lib/sandbox/builder.ts:634) stores whatever object Muse Code wrote. decideOutcome ships 'partial' whenever typecheck, build and start pass, even when the 'manifest' verify step (the schema check) failed, so a malformed manifest reaches products.manifest. The UI then uses it without guards. (a) BuildRoom.tsx:235: refine builds have no brief, so models comes from product.manifest.models.map, and a manifest without 'models' throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading map)'. Every refine build room of that product then fails during SSR. (b) p/[slug]/page.tsx:43: "limits": "None" passes the ?.length test and limits.map throws, so the product page returns 500. Objects in limits or models[].usedFor, or an object 'inspiration' (line 45), throw 'Objects are not valid as a React child'. (c) queries.ts:302 copies a non-string manifest.inspiration into ProductCard, and truncate() calls .trim on it, which takes down /gallery for everyone. A non-array 'models' at queries.ts:294 throws inside safeQuery, so the gallery wrongly shows 'Can't reach the database'.
suggestedFix: Validate the manifest against a zod schema in registerStep, the same one that matches template/musemuse.schema.json, and store null or the sanitized parts when it fails. In the UI, guard with Array.isArray(manifest?.models), Array.isArray(manifest?.limits), and typeof manifest?.inspiration === 'string' before using them.
fixNotes: In registerStep, validate the manifest before storing it. Use a zod schema that mirrors template/musemuse.schema.json, or at least check Array.isArray(models/limits/actions/fixtures) and typeof inspiration/tagline === 'string'. Store only the fields that pass, or skip the manifest update. Add Array.isArray guards at BuildRoom.tsx:235, p/[slug]/page.tsx:40-45 and queries.ts:294/302.

title: The build room decides who may refine from the build's userId, not the product owner
failureScenario: canRefine is user.id === data.build.userId, but the messages route allows refinement by product.ownerId, and GET /api/builds/[id] reports isOwner from product.ownerId. Example: an admin refines a tester's product to fix it, so the new refine build's userId is the admin's. That build is now history[0], and the owner opens it from the product page's Refine link once it ships. canRefine is false there, so the owner never sees the composer for their own product again, even though the API would accept their request.
suggestedFix: Compute canRefine as user.isAdmin || user.id === data.product?.ownerId. Fall back to build.userId only when there is no product yet.
fixNotes: Use canRefine = Boolean(user && (user.isAdmin || user.id === (data.product?.ownerId ?? data.build.userId))).

title: The admin kill switch is silently undone when a build of that product finishes
failureScenario: StatusControl, which shows for admins on any product page including 'building' products, sets products.status = 'disabled' and says 'Turning a product off also stops its gateway token.' But registerStep sets status: input.status ('live' or 'partial') with no condition, and it is wired to a newly minted live token. Example: an admin turns off a product while its first build or an in-flight refinement is still running. When that build ships, the product is live again with a fresh live token, and the UI never says the kill was reverted.
suggestedFix: In registerStep, add a condition that leaves status alone when it is 'disabled' (for example, set status with CASE WHEN status = 'disabled' THEN status ELSE $new END), and revoke the new live token in that case. Alternatively, stop in-flight builds when an admin disables the product.
fixNotes: In registerStep's update, keep 'disabled': set status: sql`case when ${schema.products.status} = 'disabled' then ${schema.products.status} else ${input.status} end`. Or read the status first, and if it is disabled, skip the status change and revoke the new live token.

title: After a successful refinement, the product page and gallery lose the brief
failureScenario: Refine builds never get a brief (build-steps.ts:673 notes that 'their own build rows have no brief'), but registerStep sets latestBuildId to the refine build. The product page reads brief = latestBuild?.brief, which is now null, so the 'Took from it / Left out' section disappears. Models, limits and cost per run fall back to the manifest only, so the template default shows '$0.00 est.' if Muse Code left it alone. listShippedProducts (queries.ts:286) joins the same build, so gallery cards show only the refine's duration, cost and fix rounds, for example 'Built in 2 m · $0.08'. This happens on the demo's refine step ('add a dark mode').
suggestedFix: Load the brief from the product's first build (kind = 'build') for the product page and gallery. Report build time and cost either from the original build or summed across the product's builds.
fixNotes: In getProductPage, also load the brief from the product's newest kind='build' build (the same query as latestBrief in build-steps.ts) and use it for brief. In listShippedProducts, join that original build for brief, buildMs and fixRounds, or sum cost across the product's builds.
